questions.question: When driving down a steep hill, your brakes may fade. What does brake fade mean?

options.text: They become quieter.
They become less effective.
They work better than usual.
They work differently from front to back.

questions.correctAnswerText: They become less effective.
questions.explanation: Using your brakes too much on a steep downhill can overheat them, making them less effective. To prevent this, use engine braking on steep hills.

questions.question: When should you adjust your mirrors?

options.text: While moving.
When the trailer is straight.
When you are standing next to the vehicle.
By an assistant.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the trailer is straight.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors before starting a trip. If you have a trailer, you can only adjust mirrors correctly when the trailer is straight.

questions.question: What is the best way to reduce cell phone distractions while driving?

options.text: Stay on a single call for the entire trip.
Turn the phone off before driving.
Only use the phone to accept incoming calls.
Use the phone to text instead of talk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the phone off before driving.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid cell phone distractions is to turn it off before you start driving and keep it off until you reach your destination.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a cause of hydraulic brake failure?

options.text: Loss of hydraulic pressure
Brake fade on long hills
Downshifting

questions.correctAnswerText: Downshifting
questions.explanation: Hydraulic brake failure is caused by loss of hydraulic pressure or overuse on long hills that causes brake fade. Downshifting does not cause hydraulic brake failure.

questions.question: If you see taillights ahead while driving in fog, what should you know?

options.text: The lights may not show where the road is. The vehicle may have left the roadway.
You can assume the vehicle is on the road.
The lights may be an optical illusion.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lights may not show where the road is. The vehicle may have left the roadway.
questions.explanation: In fog, vehicle lights are not reliable guides to the road. A vehicle with lights on may have left the road.

questions.question: What is true about hydroplaning?

options.text: It only happens at very high speeds.
It can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph.
It happens most when tire pressure is too high.
It happens most when tires have good tread.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning can occur at speeds as low as 30 mph if there is enough water on the road. It is most likely when tire pressure is too low or tire tread is worn.

questions.question: What is the maximum air leakage rate for a double combination vehicle during an applied leakage test?

options.text: 2 psi in one minute
4 psi in one minute
6 psi in one minute

questions.correctAnswerText: 4 psi in one minute
questions.explanation: A double combination vehicle must not lose more than 4 psi of air pressure in one minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: While driving, if you notice a safety or mechanical problem, what should you do?

options.text: Stay quiet and hope it goes away.
Make a written report of your concerns.
Try to fix the issue yourself.
Avoid using that part and hope others don't notice.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make a written report of your concerns.
questions.explanation: At the end of each driving day, write a report about any safety or mechanical issues. This helps prevent accidents and breakdowns.

questions.question: What is true about dual tires?

options.text: They should not both touch the road.
They should not touch each other.
They should be different sizes.

questions.correctAnswerText: They should not touch each other.
questions.explanation: When inspecting your vehicle, make sure your dual tires do not touch each other or any other part of the vehicle.

questions.question: While driving, how should you use your mirrors?

options.text: Do not use them.
Use them only when changing lanes.
Check them regularly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check them regularly.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly while driving to stay aware of traffic around you and spot possible problems on your vehicle.

questions.question: When checking power steering fluid during a vehicle inspection, which of the following is NOT required?

options.text: Show where the power steering fluid dipstick is located.
Check that there is enough power steering fluid.
Make sure the power steering fluid level is above the full mark.
Make sure the power steering level is above the refill mark.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the power steering fluid level is above the full mark.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must show where the power steering fluid dipstick is located and prove there is enough fluid in the engine compartment. The fluid level must be above the refill mark, not above the full mark.

questions.question: Emergency equipment in a vehicle is:

options.text: Only required for vehicles carrying hazardous materials.
Only required for interstate driving.
Required for all vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required for all vehicles.
questions.explanation: All vehicles must have emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, three red reflective triangles or flares, and at least one fire extinguisher that is charged and rated properly.

questions.question: Air tank drains are used to:

options.text: Allow rainwater to enter the tanks.
Drain water and oil from the air tanks.
Stay closed at all times.
Stay open while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drain water and oil from the air tanks.
questions.explanation: Compressed air contains water and compressor oil. These can damage the brakes if they build up. You must open the air tank drains daily to remove this buildup.

questions.question: On a passenger bus, carry-on baggage must:

options.text: Be placed in the aisle.
Be stored away from the aisle.
Be kept on a rider's lap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be stored away from the aisle.
questions.explanation: Baggage cannot block doorways or aisles. It must be secured so it does not damage, block the driver's movement, block emergency exits, or injure passengers if it falls or shifts.

questions.question: Pressing and releasing the brake pedal unnecessarily can:

options.text: Release air faster than it can be replaced.
Add more air to the brake system.
Make the brake pedal harder to press.
Create loud noise.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release air faster than it can be replaced.
questions.explanation: In a vehicle with air brakes, pressing and releasing the brake pedal too much can release air faster than the compressor can replace it. This lowers air pressure and can cause the brakes to fail.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a recommended way to spot trouble?

options.text: Watch the gauges.
Use your senses.
Check critical items only at the start and end of a trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check critical items only at the start and end of a trip.
questions.explanation: Check your vehicle regularly during a trip, not just at the beginning and end. Check the instrument panel, mirrors, tires, cargo, and lights. Use all your senses to catch problems early.

questions.question: If you pull to the side of the road, you should:

options.text: Let your taillights warn other drivers.
Turn on your emergency flashers to warn other drivers.
Keep your lights off to avoid distracting other drivers.
Keep your door open to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your emergency flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: Always turn on your emergency flashers when stopped on the roadside, especially at night. Taillights alone may not be enough—other drivers may think you are moving normally and hit you.

questions.question: Mirrors should be:

options.text: Checked only when changing lanes.
Checked often.
Checked only if you suspect a problem.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checked often.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly while driving. This helps you know what traffic is around you and watch for problems with your own vehicle.

questions.question: What is a danger of rolling backward when you start to accelerate?

options.text: The transmission may be damaged.
The truck cannot go backward.
You may hit a vehicle behind you.
You may lose your position in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may hit a vehicle behind you.
questions.explanation: Prevent your vehicle from rolling backward when starting from a stop. If your vehicle has a manual transmission, partly engage the clutch before releasing the brake.

questions.question: Very hot temperatures can cause:

options.text: Tire failure.
A trailer to disconnect.
Lights to stop working.
Better gas mileage.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tire failure.
questions.explanation: Hot air expands, which increases tire pressure. This can cause tire failure. Check your tire pressure regularly when driving in hot weather.
